kjv: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid
mine: Spread the corner of your garment over your servant
note: kenafekha means "your wing / the corner of your garment", a marriage gesture (cf. Ezek 16:8). It deliberately echoes 2:12, "under whose wings you have come to take refuge".

kjv: and she went into the city
mine: Then he went into the city
note: The MT has the masculine wayyavo' (Boaz went). The KJV's "she" follows some Hebrew manuscripts and the Vulgate and Syriac versions.

mine: How did it go, my daughter?
note: mi-'at bitti, literally "who are you?", is probably idiomatic here: "how do you stand?", that is, are you now betrothed? The KJV's literal rendering is puzzling, since Naomi knows who she is.
